points.title: Shop sentences, not pronoun rules
points.rule: Ask the price with cuesta. Point with esto. Me lo llevo and puedo probarme are fixed sentences. Hay means there is. The shop may say tiene, quiere, or le ayudo. Answer with busco, puedo, and pago. ¿Dónde está el probador? reuses está from day 8. Solo estoy mirando reuses estoy from day 11.

grammar.notYet: Object pronouns and este, esta, and estos. Leave me lo llevo whole.

phrases.english: Do you have a bigger size?
phrases.note: Tiene is what you say to shop staff. Tienes is for a friend.
Say the question whole. Point with esto.
One fixed sentence. Do not split lo.

phrases.english: I am looking for a blue shirt.

phrases.note: This is what the shop asks you.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Sí. Busco una chaqueta. ¿Cuánto cuesta esto?
lines.english: Yes. I am looking for a jacket. How much does this cost?

lines.speaker: Dependienta
lines.english: It costs forty euros. What size do you wear?

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.english: Medium. Can I try this on?

lines.speaker: Dependienta
lines.spanish: Claro. El probador está a la derecha.
lines.english: Of course. The fitting room is on the right.

lines.speaker: Alex
lines.spanish: Me queda bien. Me lo llevo. Pago con tarjeta.
lines.english: It fits well. I’ll take it. I’ll pay by card.

practice.title: Buy something
practice.instruction: Role-play buying a shirt or a coffee. Ask the price, the size or the options, then pay.
starters: Me lo llevo. Pago con tarjeta.
tips: Five phrases are enough for a shop.
If the number is fast, ask: ¿Puede repetir, por favor?
